**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is a square-ish white side plate, about 20 cm across. Treating it as a 20 cm round equivalent gives an area of 3.14 × (10)² ≈ 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** One item is visible: a compact pile of dark green wilted leaves with a few stems. No oil, dressing, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The leaf pile covers roughly 10% of the plate, about 31 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is about 2 cm high on average, so 31 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 60 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Loose, wilted leafy greens have a bulk density of about 0.2 g/ml, so 60 ml × 0.2 ≈ 12 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked spinach is about 23 kcal per 100 g, so 12 g × 0.23 ≈ 3 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A few wilted leaves on a side plate should weigh only tens of grams or less, and 12 g and 3 kcal fit that. The total is plausible.
